A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cake system, with matching authors and central design. The text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v1 Appendices A–C and v2 Appendices A–B, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original latency, resource-utilization and compression experiments in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix C, using synthetic prompts and simulated I/O conditions.

after.justification: V2 reports original system evaluations in Tables 3–6 and Figures 5–7, including model-architecture comparisons, fluctuating-resource traces and adaptive-scheduling results.

M1.justification: The bidirectional loader remains, but v2 adds an explicit scheduling mode prioritizing decoding, uncached prefill and then cached prefill, extending v1's spare-budget discussion. Appendix A also replaces the shared chunk-size parameter with separate compute and fetch chunk sizes. These change the scheduling procedure.

E1.justification: Both use synthetic prompts motivated by LongChat, TriviaQA and NarrativeQA. V2 extends serving scenarios to a burst of short uncached requests competing with a long cached request (Section 5.7), and jointly fluctuating compute and I/O availability. The underlying language-task domains remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Compute-only, I/O-only and 8-bit comparisons remain. V1's CacheGen compression comparisons in Figure 6 and Appendix C are replaced by 3-bit quantization attributed to KVQuant in v2 Table 6. V2 Figure 4 also adds an SSD-loading curve to the corresponding per-chunk GPU comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA 3.1-8B/70B configurations, FP8 weights for the 70B model and two-A100 tensor parallelism, and revises bandwidth and utilization grids. Main-evaluation prompt sampling changes from 20 lengths within 5–16K plus 32K stress tests to 4–16K lengths at 2K intervals. New protocols evaluate simultaneous resource fluctuations and mixed-request throughput.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the resource, length and compression sensitivity studies, adds MHA-versus-GQA analysis, tests jointly fluctuating resources and compares default versus adaptive scheduling under bursty arrivals (Sections 5.4–5.7). The per-step integration-overhead analysis remains in Figure 7.

E5.justification: V1 displays error bars throughout its performance sweeps, including Figures 5b, 6, 8b and Appendix C, although their meaning and run counts are unspecified. V2's replacement result tables provide point estimates without corresponding uncertainty. Section 5.2 additionally introduces exclusion of cases exceeding 10x speedup before averaging.

E6.justification: Most v1 latency and compression sweeps are replaced by results under revised settings in Tables 3–6. New findings include a 0.80x speedup against I/O-only for LLaMA 3.1-70B at 12.5% utilization and 32 Gbps on two A100s, and a scheduling experiment reducing completion time from 1.5 to 1.19 seconds. These are new comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V1 Section 3's explicit KV-cache-size equation and accompanying numerical calculation are removed. V2 introduces standard attention equations as background explanation, without adding a theorem or proof. The substantive mathematical change is therefore limited.

C1.justification: V2 elevates adaptive scheduling and improved mixed-request throughput to central contributions, including a 26% throughput claim. Its headline performance claim becomes an average 2.6x TTFT reduction, replacing v1's maximum reductions of 68.1% versus computation and 94.6% versus I/O. The central bidirectional-loading contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 explains why balanced resources favor Cake and acknowledges cases where scheduling overhead makes it slower than a baseline, proposing a single-resource fallback as future work (Sections 5.2–5.4). This qualifies v1's consistent-superiority narrative. V1's argument that computing only 75% of tokens saves 25% of GPU cache memory is also removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies vLLM 0.6.2 and LMCache 0.1.4 versions, explicit cache and weight precisions, model-configuration tables and the 128-token fetching setting. Appendix A clarifies cached-prefix hash lookup. Appendix B largely retains the implementation description, while changing the documented retrieval API from push_seq to batch_retrieve.

R1.justification: V2 adds a structured Related Work section covering quantization, pruning, architectural compression and hierarchical cache management. New cited coverage includes GQA, KIVI, ScissorHands and H2O, while earlier Hydragen and Prompt Cache coverage disappears. It also explicitly positions Cake as the first system jointly exploiting computation and I/O for this purpose.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and background are extensively rewritten. V2 adds Related Work, integrates exploratory motivation into Design, reorganizes Evaluation and removes the standalone Discussion and Ethics Statement sections. Appendices A and B are retained with limited edits, while Appendix C disappears.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column layout, adds Tables 1–6 and replaces numerous latency plots and Appendix C panels with tabular comparisons. Retained diagrams are relocated or renumbered. The memory display changes from cumulative GB in v1 Figure 3 to constant per-chunk MB in v2 Figure 4, alongside an added SSD curve.

improvement.justification: Broader architecture and hardware testing, mixed-request evaluation and explicit failure cases make Cake's practical applicability clearer than v1's consistent-superiority narrative. These gains are tempered by the loss of error bars and numerical reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.2 quotes a 2.23x H100 speedup at 100% utilization and 32 Gbps, whereas Table 3 reports 2.40x. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
